sourceDigestNormalization: UTF-8 source bytes with CRLF normalized to LF

original-repair-files-final.json.durationMs: parallel file durations are not summed

coverage: The helper acquires a source purge fence, rejects live/unknown source file leases and uses an immutable context-bound intent before writing private candidate bytes.

Candidate chunks are hashed in bounded memory, checked for full expected SHA/size/PDF header and fsynced before exclusive hard-link publication. Each critical publication invokes a required caller guard.

The old known inode/bytes are retained through an exclusive hard link before original unlink. Interrupted retries recognize original-plus-retained, retained-only, correct-published and cleaned states. Unknown replacement/candidate/retained bytes and links are preserved.
An absent or different immutable intent cannot authorize pruning private candidate staging. Dead producer names are checked twice before known pending files are removed.

Fifteen real Node SIGKILL boundaries, a competing live writer/live reader, explicit guard revocation injections, corrupt chunks/header, changed external original/candidate/retained files, altered binding, unknown files, junction substitution and upload loss after successful publication are covered.
Latest 26 file-protocol tests plus 23 existing atomic-publication and 5 file-coordination cases pass. The initial 25-case run also passed.
diagnostics: An initial TypeScript nullability failure in staged-name parsing was corrected before runtime validation.

Initial 5MiB Buffer deep equality used 418.5 seconds for 25 tests. It was replaced with full byte-wise Buffer.equals assertions, retaining equality scope; the latest 54-case combination completed in 15.9 seconds.
An ownership-checked attempt to stop the slow test found it already exited and did not terminate any process. The initial run completed successfully and remains archived.
limits: This is an unconnected file helper, not a usable repair endpoint or workbench feature. Required guard callbacks in this suite simulate the future task/authorization checks.
Durable repair records, repairing asset state, real permissions/revocation/privacy, maintenance/audit/backup integration, task receipts and both workbench flows remain unimplemented.
The fixtures contain a PDF header and 5MiB byte payload. Actual 120-page PDF processing and end-to-end repair must be verified after product integration.
Only process interruption is tested, not hardware power loss or an adversarial concurrent same-user filesystem writer.
Existing Node/Python coordination tests ran; no new PostgreSQL or live browser acceptance is claimed.
Production and the main worktree were not switched; the isolated PostgreSQL cluster remains stopped.
